profile.campus: Digital Fortress Portland/Beaverton cluster (acquired from Atmosera, Jan 2021, with PTL2 and PTL3)
profile.address: 511, Southwest 10th Avenue, Downtown, Portland, Multnomah County, Oregon, 97205
profile.reading:
Digital Fortress Portland 1, facility code PTL, is a Digital Fortress data center in downtown Portland, Oregon, about 12 miles from Portland International Airport by the operator's own account. Digital Fortress's own dedicated page for this facility describes 6,700 square feet of raised floor data center space with 2.1 megawatts of power capacity, and states the building is adjacent to the Pittock Block Carrier Hotel, which the operator describes as the second most connected building in the Pacific Northwest, with 16 fiber optic carriers and 179 service providers connected on site and membership in the Northwest Access Exchange. The same page describes connections to the Westin Building Exchange in Seattle and the Seattle Internet Exchange, separate physical feeds into the building for carrier diversity, and direct cloud on-ramps to major providers including AWS.

The operator's own page lists SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II compliance and describes biometric scan, key card, and CCTV physical security. It also states the facility offers a range of deployment options from single racks and cabinets to private cages and full floors, describing its customer base as ranging from startups to Fortune 500 companies, and frames the three-building Portland-area cluster, this facility plus its two Beaverton siblings in this registry, as providing redundancy and replication across sites for customers who need it.

A separate Digital Fortress press release dated January 19, 2021, published on the operator's own site, documents that Digital Fortress acquired this facility along with two sibling Beaverton, Oregon buildings in this registry, Portland 2 and Portland 3, from Atmosera Inc's colocation business, transferring more than 100 colocation customers in the deal. The press release describes the region's data center advantage as direct access to seven subsea cables, positioning the Portland area as a connectivity gateway to Asia Pacific markets.

No confirmed street address for this specific building has been found in Digital Fortress's own materials. The address on file here comes from a reverse geocode of this registry's stored coordinates rather than an operator or government primary source, and should be treated as an approximation pending stronger corroboration, though it is consistent with the operator's own description of a downtown Portland location adjacent to the Pittock Block. Digital Fortress is a colocation data center operator and a portfolio company of Chirisa Investments, which also owns the Piscataway, New Jersey, Richmond, Virginia, and Lynnwood, Washington facilities already on file elsewhere in this registry under the same operator.

reading.body:
Digital Fortress Portland 1 is a 2.1 megawatt colocation facility in downtown Portland with 6,700 square feet of raised floor space. Assuming 40 kilowatts per rack as a common density for mixed workloads, this capacity could accommodate roughly 50 racks. The facility is one of three in a Portland-area cluster operated by Digital Fortress, positioned to serve customers ranging from startups to Fortune 500 companies with deployment options from single racks to full floors.

The site's relevance to AI compute is its connectivity rather than its scale. The adjacent Pittock Block Carrier Hotel hosts 16 fiber carriers and 179 service providers, and the facility advertises direct feeds to major cloud providers including AWS, separate physical carrier diversity paths, and cross-city redundancy links to Seattle. The operator frames the three-building cluster as providing replication for customers needing it. Portland itself sits on seven subsea cables, which the operator describes as a gateway to Asia Pacific markets, but this single facility's 2.1 megawatt capacity is too small to move the needle on regional or national AI infrastructure.

At 2.1 megawatts of published capacity, Digital Fortress Portland 1 ranks ninth among the eight facilities with published figures in Oregon and accounts for roughly 1.3 percent of the state's 156.6 megawatts of published data center capacity. Oregon has 133 mapped facilities total but only eight publish power figures, meaning most capacity in the state is undisclosed. This facility matters for redundancy and interconnection in its market segment but not for AI scaling at any meaningful scale.
